The engine was right and unreachable, which is its own kind of absent. The WHOLE network is sent and judged at once, because a cycle is a property of the graph and never of one edge: an endpoint taking edges singly could be walked into a loop one individually-legal step at a time. Everything is refused rather than repaired — a self-edge, a duplicate, an edge naming an activity outside this plan, and a cycle whose loop is named back to the author — because which of two activities waits for the other is a decision and not arithmetic, and a refused save is never a partial save. Authoring the network carries `projects.schedule.plan`: it decides what the solver may move and what the critical path runs through. Deleting an activity takes its edges with it rather than leaving the network pointing at a task that no longer exists. The accepted dates FOLLOW the network, stepping over the days the project’s own calendar says are not worked (PLN-03), so a successor never starts on a Friday the crew was never asked to work.

capabilities.currentBehavior: A schedule activity now reads what its work package was SOLD and PRICED for, and nobody types either. The rate the line was priced at is frozen with the award: at handover the accepted line’s rate build-up is read once and its manpower sheet normalised to ONE unit — crew size, man-hours per unit, crew-hours per unit — so a later revision selling a different quantity cannot distort it. IT CARRIES NO MONEY: hourly rates, margin and every amount stay behind `tendering.internal-pricing.access`, because how long work takes is a physical fact about the work while what it costs is a commercial one, and freezing the second would put the cost sheet inside every project anyone can open. Delivery then reaches back into Tendering for nothing — the basis is copied by value like every other award fact. On the read, an activity resolves the sold quantity, the priced rate, the quantity installed through the Quantity Ledger and the part of its own planned window already used, and reports the pace the work is going at against the pace it was sold at, with the rate now needed to still finish inside the window. Everything is DERIVED per read and stored nowhere: a stored “behind” would be behind as of the last refresh. UNKNOWN is neither zero nor “on rate” — a package with no award line, an award captured before the basis was frozen, a supply-only or subcontracted line that priced no crew, an activity with no usable window and a window that has not opened each come back UNKNOWN carrying the reason, while every fact that IS known is still reported beside it. The plan screen shows what was sold against what is in, the pace against the priced pace, and a headline count of the activities losing ground; an activity with no award line behind it stays silent rather than printing “unknown” under every bar. THE COST HALF IS NOW CONNECTED TOO. A labour allocation carries the work package its hours were spent on (migration 0323), checked at the service boundary through the resolver Projects registers at boot — a package in another project is refused at the point of writing, not discovered later by a report that drops the row. Projects reads those hours through a port bound at the composition root (ADR-0004), never importing Site, and sets three quantities of hours apart: PRICED (per unit, frozen with the award), EARNED (priced × installed — what the work should have taken) and SPENT (what the people who were there wrote down). The factor is earned ÷ spent, and it is a SEPARATE verdict from the pace, deliberately: a crew can be behind the programme and perfectly efficient, or exactly on rate and ruinous, and one number cannot carry both. NULL ATTRIBUTION IS NORMAL AND PERMANENT — mobilisation, standing time, a crew moving between three risers — so the share of the project’s hours naming no package travels WITH every figure, because a package credited with 40 of 500 man-hours looks superb until somebody is told about the other 460. No hours attributed at all reads UNKNOWN, never as infinite productivity, and hours spent before the first measure read UNKNOWN rather than a productivity of zero.

capabilities.currentBehavior: An activity’s progress is resolved on every read from three states kept apart by name and never stored as one number. EVIDENCE is the work package’s measured progress, derived through the Quantity Ledger from quantity installed against the frozen sold item; it is not copied onto the activity, because a copy is only correct as of the last refresh. DECLARED is a plain number where nothing has been measured at all: unchanged in behaviour and now labelled rather than passing for measurement. An override exists only where evidence does, so a typed figure can never acquire a reason and a signature it did not earn. Saving a plan can neither mint a statement nor drop one — the four override fields are resolved from the persisted activity and ignored off the payload. A measured zero and a declared zero are rendered as the different facts they are, and UNKNOWN is never drawn as 0. capabilities.currentBehavior: The plan screen carries a dated, resource-aware look-ahead over the accepted programme — two to six weeks, chosen by the planner. It is a WINDOW over the plan and not a document beside it: nothing on it is authored, it is derived on every read and stored nowhere, and an edit to the programme changes the next read. That is the point. A look-ahead kept as its own artefact disagrees with the programme the first time anybody extends an activity, and the site meeting is then held against a plan that no longer exists. Each activity carries the part of ITSELF that falls inside the window in working days under the project’s calendar — four months of work is not four months of work in the next three weeks — and is marked as new work or carried in. READY IS ESTABLISHED, NEVER ASSUMED: an activity is ready only when its predecessors finish before it starts, every resource it needs is a held commitment, and every commitment is feasible. An uncommitted resource, an over-committed one and a predecessor that does not clear in time each keep it out in words a planner can act on; a resource whose capacity nobody declared reads NOT ESTABLISHED rather than ready, because “we could not find a problem” and “there is no problem” are different statements and a look-ahead that rounds the first to the second sends a crew to a site that is not open. A RELEASED booking stops being a commitment, so the activity it covered reads as uncommitted again. Scope in the window aggregates BY WORK PACKAGE and never by activity: several activities may deliver one package and each reads that package’s whole sold quantity, so a per-activity total would report the same 200 m² twice — the package contributes one row and the activities are named on it.
capabilities.acceptanceProof: Auth-ON browser and HTTP proof: a three-week window from today reporting its own working days under the project’s calendar; an activity four months out excluded and a longer window still excluding it; an uncommitted crew keeping an activity NOT READY in words; declaring capacity and committing the requirement turning the same activity READY with no reasons; releasing that booking taking the readiness with it; a predecessor that does not clear in time naming itself, and reversing the edge making the activity ready again — derived, not stored; a work package delivered by two activities contributing exactly one scope row; and an activity dragged into the window by an edit to the programme appearing on the next read with nothing authored. capabilities.currentBehavior: A delay event names the ACTIVITIES it hit, canonically (migration 0325). It has carried a WBS code as free text since it was introduced — a label that drifts the first time somebody renumbers a package, and a link no query can follow, which is not a basis for a contractual instrument. That column stays as the note it always was and is deliberately not migrated: nobody can map free text onto an activity id after the fact, and guessing would manufacture the lineage this exists to make real. TWO FACTS ARE KEPT APART because an EOT dispute is precisely the confusion of them: CLAIMED is how long the event lasted, a fact about the world; IMPACT is how many working days completion actually moved, a fact about the plan. A ten-day storm on an activity with float moves completion by less, or by nothing. A contractor claims the first, an employer grants the second, and a system reporting only one has taken a side. The impact is derived by running the SAME CPM twice — as planned, and with the delay inserted — and diffing the finishes, so the project has one answer to “when does this finish” rather than a bespoke delay calculator beside the planner. Counted in WORKING days under the project’s calendar (PLN-03): a figure in calendar days is indefensible the moment the contract is not, and a storm over a weekend nobody was going to work delayed nothing. ‘Absorbed by float’ is a real verdict rather than a failure to reach one. CONCURRENCY IS NAMED AND NEVER APPORTIONED — an overlapping delay is reported with its cause and left there, because whether it reduces liability is a question of contract and law decided by people, and halving a figure on that basis would be inventing a legal position inside arithmetic. The ASSESSMENT is a separate, recorded act: a figure, a name and a moment, stored beside the derived impact and never instead of it, so a number submitted against the plan as it then stood survives the plan moving. Zero is accepted — it is the commonest honest answer. Assessing carries `projects.delay.assess`, which a Planning Engineer holds and which does not carry the commercial decision on the claim.
